context: The Active Prompt requests implementation of a tiered contextual help system with tooltips, page-level help modals, and accessibility features. While the prompt provides clear scope and technical constraints, several design decisions require clarification to ensure the implementation aligns with user expectations and workflow patterns.

questions.question-text: Where should the help icon be positioned in the navbar for optimal visibility and consistency?

options.label: Next to the page title on the left side of the navbar
options.pros: Immediately visible next to related content, maintains left-to-right reading flow, groups help with page context
options.cons: May crowd the left side of navbar, could interfere with long page titles on mobile

options.label: On the right side of the navbar as a standalone icon
options.pros: Standard pattern for utility actions, keeps left side clean for navigation, more space for icon on mobile
options.cons: Separated from page title context, requires eye movement across navbar

options.label: As a floating button in the bottom-right corner of the page (fixed position)
options.pros: Always accessible regardless of scroll position, common help pattern, doesn't impact navbar layout
options.cons: May obscure content, separate pattern from navbar icons, requires different implementation

questions.recommendation-rationale: Positioning the help icon next to the page title creates a clear association between the help content and the current page context, which aligns with the prompt's emphasis on contextual help. This placement follows common UX patterns where help icons appear near the content they explain.

questions.question-text: How should tooltips behave on touch devices (mobile/tablet)?

options.label: Show on first tap, dismiss on second tap or tap outside
options.pros: Standard mobile pattern, allows reading tooltip without dismissing it accidentally, clear interaction model
options.cons: Requires two taps to activate a button (first for tooltip, second for action), may frustrate users in a hurry

options.label: Show on long press (tap and hold), dismiss on release
options.pros: Doesn't interfere with button clicks, similar to desktop hover behavior, familiar pattern from mobile OS
options.cons: Less discoverable than tap, users may not know to long-press, timing can be inconsistent

options.label: Replace tooltips with small info icons next to buttons that open popover on tap
options.pros: Clear visual affordance that help is available, doesn't interfere with primary actions, mobile-friendly tap targets
options.cons: Requires additional UI elements (info icons), increases visual complexity, different pattern from desktop

questions.recommendation-rationale: Bootstrap 5's native tooltip behavior supports tap-to-show on touch devices, making Option A the most consistent choice with the technical constraint of using Bootstrap components. This approach requires minimal custom code and provides a familiar interaction pattern that mobile users understand.

questions.question-text: What content should the 'Link to full user guide' in help modals point to?

options.label: External documentation URL (e.g., GitHub wiki or docs site)
options.pros: Centralized documentation, easy to update without code changes, can include rich media and search
options.cons: Requires external site setup, users must leave the app, may be slow or unavailable offline

options.label: Local README.md file opened in a new tab/window
options.pros: No external dependencies, works offline, documentation versioned with code
options.cons: Limited formatting in browser, may need route to serve markdown as HTML, harder to navigate large docs

options.label: Dedicated Help page within the Web UI with navigation sidebar
options.pros: Consistent UI/UX with rest of application, full control over presentation, works offline, can include interactive examples
options.cons: Significant development effort beyond Tier 1 scope, adds complexity to Web UI, content management overhead

options.label: Placeholder '#' for now (Tier 1 doesn't implement the full guide, only the link structure)
options.pros: Allows focusing on Tier 1 help features without committing to documentation infrastructure, can be implemented in future tier
options.cons: Broken/non-functional link frustrates users, provides no value until implemented

questions.recommendation-rationale: Since the RDD framework already includes a comprehensive README.md file (per files-and-folders.md), linking to it provides immediate value without additional infrastructure. The Web UI can add a simple route to serve the README as HTML, balancing implementation effort with user value for Tier 1.

questions.question-text: Should help tooltips for execution mode buttons include example use cases or only functional descriptions?

options.label: Functional descriptions only (e.g., 'Generate questions to resolve ambiguities')
options.pros: Concise and quick to read, fits tooltip format better, less text to maintain, faster to comprehend
options.cons: May not help new users understand when to use each mode, requires prior understanding of workflow

options.label: Functional description with one brief example (e.g., 'Clarify: Generate questions to resolve ambiguities. Use when prompt lacks specific details like file paths or behavior.')
options.pros: Helps new users understand practical application, provides context for decision-making, teaches by example
options.cons: Longer tooltips may be cut off or harder to read, requires more careful writing, can become outdated

options.label: Functional description with 'Learn more' link to expand full details in modal
options.pros: Keeps tooltip concise while offering deeper explanation, progressive disclosure for different user levels
options.cons: Requires additional modal implementation, extra click to access full information, more complex interaction

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly requests 'One-sentence description of when to use the mode and what it produces', which aligns with Option B's approach of combining functional description with a brief contextual example. This provides the most value within the tooltip format constraint.

questions.question-text: How should the help modal be styled to maintain visual consistency with the rest of the Web UI?

options.label: Standard Bootstrap modal with default styling (white background, rounded corners, shadow)
options.pros: Minimal CSS needed, consistent with Bootstrap conventions, familiar to users, works across themes
options.cons: May not match custom color scheme mentioned in prompt, generic appearance

options.label: Bootstrap modal with custom color accents matching the Web UI theme (blue headers, muted text)
options.pros: Consistent with existing UI elements mentioned in requirements (color-coded feedback), professional appearance, reinforces brand
options.cons: Requires inspecting existing CSS to match colors, slight additional styling effort

options.label: Completely custom modal design with unique styling
options.pros: Full creative control, can optimize layout specifically for help content
options.cons: Significant additional CSS/HTML work beyond Tier 1 scope, may break responsive behavior, harder to maintain

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt specifies using Bootstrap 5 components and mentions 'Follow existing color scheme (use .text-muted for help text)', indicating that customization to match the existing theme is expected. This balances consistency requirements with the constraint of minimal implementation effort.

questions.question-text: What level of detail should status flag tooltips provide?

options.label: Brief label only (e.g., 'Questionnaire Generated')
options.pros: Quick to scan, doesn't overwhelm user, suitable for users familiar with the workflow
options.cons: Doesn't explain what the flag means or how it got set, minimal educational value

options.label: Label with explanation and trigger action (e.g., 'Questionnaire Generated: Set when clarify mode completes. Indicates questionnaire.json file exists.')
options.pros: Educates users about workflow mechanics, helps troubleshooting, provides complete context
options.cons: Longer tooltips may be harder to read quickly, more text to maintain, potential for information overload

options.label: Label with explanation only, no technical details (e.g., 'Questionnaire Generated: Questions are ready for you to answer')
options.pros: User-friendly language, focuses on user actions rather than system mechanics, easier to understand
options.cons: Less useful for understanding the workflow state machine, may not help with debugging issues

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt requests 'Explain what each flag means and what action sets it', which directly aligns with Option B. This level of detail supports the prompt's goal of helping users learn the framework's workflow model without external documentation.
